text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office stores correspondence, ledgers, and case files by date and category. Entries are indexed by reference number, actor, and date, with cross-references linking related documents within the same filing system.

2) What occurred: The actor drafted a dated written proposal containing a sum-of-money figure, delivered through a personal message channel to a named recipient holding an inspector role. The actor opened a named bank account and executed a dated wire transfer of a monetary figure to an account registered to a third party. The actor altered a field in an inspection record, changing its status value from "violation noted" to "compliant," and stamped a date earlier than the recorded visit date. The actor created a supplementary memo attributed to the named inspector, filed in the same case folder as the inspection record.

3) Materials/access observed: One written proposal document; one personal message thread between the actor and the named inspector; one bank transaction record from a named account; one inspection case file with a modified status field and an out-of-sequence date stamp; one memo bearing the inspector's name.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Date inconsistency between the inspection visit date and the amended record stamp; a payment trail terminating at an account not affiliated with the building authority; an unsigned memo filed post-closure of the original case; a status-field edit with no corresponding audit log entry; correspondence between the actor and inspector predating the inspection date.
